results.name: W1 corpus: every readable docx rewritten with WordprocessingML prefix q (and in default-namespace form) reads to the SAME model as the original; the TT71 reader opened none of the prefix rewrites
W2 lxml: every WordprocessingML part canonicalised by the reader (prefix rewrites, default-namespace forms, corpus parts that are not already canonical) is namespace-equivalent to its input

W3 round trip from a foreign-prefix document: edit → writeWord → the output re-reads to the edited model, python-docx opens it, and Track Changes on a q:-prefixed settings.xml writes a DECLARED w:trackRevisions
W4 legacy /api/office readDocx: prefix and default-namespace forms, single-quoted pStyle, numeric character references

W5 corpus: every readable docx with all word/**.xml attributes single-quoted and spaced reads to the SAME model, and the next tracked-change id stays above every existing w:id (no revision-id collisions)

W6 pictures in headers / footers / comments / notes resolve through THAT part's relationships (OPC): every picture the reader shows is one the part references — lxml + zipfile oracle over the corpus; TT71 showed the main document's rIdN

W7 one rId, four parts: body, header, comment and footnote each use rId9 for a DIFFERENT picture — each part shows its own (part rels + no cross-part media cache); TT71 showed the body's picture or styles.xml everywhere

W8 lossless no-edit save: every readable corpus docx AND its q:-prefixed rewrite saves byte-identically when unedited (canonicalised parts go back as their original bytes; Word 2007 ve: files are not rewritten)

S1 corpus: every readable xlsx with all xl/**.xml attributes single-quoted and spaced around '=' reads to the SAME model (inputs, values, styles, widths, merges, validations, links); the TT71 reader lost cells / styles on them
S2 font / fill flags: <b val='0'/> and <b val = "false"/> are not bold, <b/> and <b val='1'/> are; patternType = 'solid' fills; underline 'none' is off
P1 corpus: every readable pptx with all ppt/**.xml attributes single-quoted and spaced reads to the same deck (titles, bodies, notes); the TT71 reader differed
C1 Agile EncryptionInfo written with single quotes (same bytes length, patched inside the CFB) still decrypts with HMAC verified; TT71 refused it
